grades.reason: A heading fragment from the RISC-V crypto vector spec. It has nothing to do with condition variables or while loops.
It is about the intended audience of the BF16 extension and is unrelated to condition-variable waits.

grades.quote: piperead(pipe){ acquire(&pipe->lock); while(there’s no data in pipe->buffer){ // ZZZ sleep(&pipe, &pipe->lock); } remove the data from the pipe; release(&pipe->lock); }
grades.reason: It describes xv6 sleep/wakeup, which is a condition-wait mechanism. Its pipe example calls sleep inside a while loop that re-checks the condition, and it explains the condition lock and lost wake-ups. It never says that the loop exists to re-check the condition after waking (spurious or stolen wakeups, or wakeup waking all waiters). So it gives only limited, indirect help on why a while loop is used.
It is only a page number (118) from the condition variables section and has no content that answers the question.
